data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise linking ideas across sentences with reference words, addition, contrast, cause, result and sequence.
learningPoints: Use pronouns and reference words to avoid unnecessary repetition.
Use addition linkers such as also and in addition.
Use contrast linkers such as however and although.
Use cause and result linkers such as because and therefore.
Use sequencing expressions such as first, then and finally.
Choose cohesive devices that make relationships between ideas clear.

sections.explain: Use a pronoun to refer back clearly to a noun already mentioned.

words.word: I bought a new laptop. It is much faster than my old one.
I bought a new laptop. He is much faster than my old one.
I bought a new laptop. Laptop is much faster than my old one.
The course is useful. It is also very practical.
The course is useful. However, it is also very practical as a contrast.
The course is useful. Because it is also practical.

sections.explain: IN ADDITION introduces another supporting point.

words.word: The hotel is close to the station. In addition, it is inexpensive.
The hotel is close to the station. In contrast, it is inexpensive for the same reason.
The hotel is close to the station. Because, it is inexpensive.

sections.explain: HOWEVER introduces a contrasting idea and is normally separated by punctuation.

words.word: The job is interesting. However, the hours are long.
The job is interesting. Therefore, the hours are long as a contrast.
The job is interesting however but the hours are long.
The road was closed. Therefore, we took another route.
The road was closed. However, we took another route because this is a result.
The road was closed. Although, we took another route.

sections.explain: Use ONE/ONES to avoid repeating a countable noun when the meaning is clear.

words.word: I don't like the red shoes; I prefer the black ones.
I don't like the red shoes; I prefer the black them.
I don't like the red shoes; I prefer black one shoes.

sections.summary: Using 'this' to refer to a previous idea.
sections.explain: THIS can refer back to a whole previous situation.

words.word: The company reduced its prices. This increased sales.
The company reduced its prices. He increased sales.
The company reduced its prices. These was increased sales.

sections.explain: Sequencing devices help order events or instructions.

words.word: First, complete the form. Then send it by email.
However, complete the form. Because send it by email.
First complete the form, therefore before send it by email.
Although the room was small, it was comfortable.
Although the room was small, but it was comfortable.
Therefore the room was small, it was comfortable.

sections.explain: Choose a connector that logically follows from the first sentence.

words.word: He had missed several lessons. As a result, he found the test difficult.
He had missed several lessons. In addition, he found the test difficult as a result connector.
He had missed several lessons. Although, he found the test difficult.
